To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the histone modification patterns of homeobox gene promoters and DNA methylation patterns of homeobox loci are altered in human oral squamous cell carcinoma cells compared to normal keratinocytes.
the histone modifications and DNA methylation patterns are altered at HOX genes in human oral keratinoctyes and oral SCC cells.

1) the levels of H3 lysine 9 trimethylation (H3K9me) and H3 lysine79 trimethylation (K79) are altered at homeobox genes in SCC cells, 2) the levels of DNA methylation at homeobox gene clusters are altered in SCC cells, and 3) the levels of the H3K4 trimethylation (me3) and H3K79 trimethylation marks correlate with homeobox gene expression
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of epigenetic mechanisms in the regulation of the transcript levels of a subset of human HOX genes in oral keratinocytes and oral squamous cell carcinoma.
the role of homeobox genes in oral cavity squamous cell carcinogenesis and the role of histone modification and DNA methylation in the regulation of HOX gene expression.
understanding the molecular events that regulate the expression of homeobox genes, and how the dysregulation of these genes contributes to human oral cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

both histone modification patterns (e.g., H3K9 and H3K79 methylation) and DNA methylation are altered at the HOX gene loci in human oral squamous cell carcinoma cells, and these changes may contribute to the dysregulation of HOX gene expression in this cancer type.

the histone modification pattern is altered in the oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma cells and that the histone mark deposition and DNA methylation are correlated with the expression of homeobox genes in these cells.
the histone modifications are associated with homeobox gene expression and the expression is associated with the DNA methylation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the homeobox genes are important in oral cavity carcinomas, and that they are regulated by histone modifications and DNA methylation.
histone modification patterns are associated with DNA methylation and that both play a role in the regulation of HOX gene expression in human keratinocytes.

we have identified several histone modifications and DNA methylation patterns which correlate with homeobox gene expression and that are altered in human oral keratincytes and tongue squamous carcinoma cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression levels of homeobox genes are controlled by both histone modifications and DNA methylation, which is consistent with the findings in our previous paper.
the expression of HOX genes is altered in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCC) and that this alteration is due to both changes in histone modification and DNA methylation at HOX loci.
the expression of homeobox genes, which are important for the development of many tissues, including the oral cavity, is dysregulated in oral cancer cells.
